That's not the equation at all. What's the value of the territory you're protecting? Well, if it's the homeland, that's pretty valuable to me. And so, and also deterring an attack in the first instance and avoiding nuclear war. Anything that you can do defensively that complicates the offensive planning of the opposition, even though it may not itself be the be all and end all defense, can be useful. Make the enemy pay for a cost for the attack that he's going to engage in. And there are a lot of other things. We talk about the industrial capacity, the use of our allies, the use of cyber, hybrid warfare in our part as well, and some other technologies that I haven't talked about here. which all three nations are spending a lot of time in effort looking at. One thing John McCain wanted to do as chairman of the committee next year was to have a series of hearings on hypersonics and on quantum computing and artificial intelligence, all kinds of things that can be brought to bear in the military and are being brought to bear right now in military planning. And I'm hoping that next year that a lot of that will be not only in a classified setting but brought to the American people's attention through through public hearings so they can see what could be available if we had the ability to fund it adequately. Let me just thank all of you for your attention and plead with you to give this your attention and to support those who are supportive of the idea about putting our national defense first and being able to deter conflict from would-be adversaries. I would appreciate it very much and thank you again for your attention.
